h1: Cortexa FAQ — AI & SaaS FAQ Section Design
tagline: FAQ section reference built around “How do I start the process of buying a home?”, with the layout, timings and palette written down in the brief.
summary: FAQ section reference for an AI or SaaS product — 400ms transitions, React and Tailwind CSS, a word-by-word headline and looping video.
about: Cortexa FAQ is a working reference for an AI or SaaS product: the FAQ section laid out, measured and ready to rebuild. It leads with “How do I start the process of buying a home?” and gives that line the frame rather than shrinking it into a card. It ships as React and Tailwind CSS, so the whole FAQ section can be lifted into a project without a design handoff. Motion comes down to 400ms transitions and a looping video bed. Start from the captured brief, then edit the FAQ section rather than rebuilding it from scratch.

layout.title: Numbers carried into the build
layout.body: The layout works on absolute values rather than ratios: 15px spacing steps and 400ms transitions. A rebuild that hits those numbers looks like the reference without further tuning.

layout.title: One clip does the work
layout.body: The brief specifies the video at 1826x1302 with a loop of 0.1s, and every text element is placed against that frame. A poster frame at 1826x1302 holds the composition when autoplay is unavailable, so the layout never collapses.

layout.title: The form is the whole first screen
layout.body: There is one decision to make here: fill the form or leave. Everything else on the screen supports that decision. Labels sit above their inputs and the supporting copy stays above the first field. Specify the focus state.

layout.title: The brief names the steps
layout.body: Spacing is quoted the same way (15px spacing steps and 400ms transitions), not as a scale that grows on its own.

motion.title: Interaction kept local
motion.body: The page answers only where it can be acted on: hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card and tabs or an accordion that swaps content in place. Each state changes one property, which keeps the feedback legible. Do not animate layout on hover.

motion.title: Fast enough to feel deliberate
motion.body: State changes are specified at 400ms, so the feedback on the controls is a designed value rather than a browser default. Nothing waits on a scroll position, so the page responds the moment you touch it.

fonts.name: Face not specified
fonts.role: The brief fixes the type scale but leaves the face to the build

notes: Media is specified at 1826x1302 and a 0.1s loop, so a replacement should match the crop and the loop length.
Nothing sits between the type and the 1826x1302 clip, so a replacement has to work under the copy directly.
The clip is one asset at 1826x1302 and a 0.1s loop, so the composition has a single media dependency.

customize: Read the brief value by value against the 1826x1302 capture before you edit anything; the numbers are the part that is easiest to lose.
Swap in your own headline where “How do I start the process of buying a home?” sits and keep the line breaks, because the entrance animates per line.
Keep 1826x1302 for the media and re-crop your own asset into it rather than resizing the frame.
Retime the entrance to your own 400ms, but keep a standard ease-out as the curve, because the easing is what reads as this design.

editorial.title: What this FAQ section gets right
editorial.body: There is one promise on this page, and 15px spacing steps and 400ms transitions hold it in place. “How do I start the process of buying a home?” is doing that work from the first frame. Nothing below the fold is asked to carry the offer as well. It gives a SaaS reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

editorial.title: How Cortexa FAQ sequences the first read
editorial.body: You could shuffle these blocks and the page would still load. It would stop reading as an argument, though: the form are a sequence, and 15px spacing steps and 400ms transitions only work in that order. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: How the FAQ section reflows
editorial.body: The desktop composition is solved against 1826x1302, and the narrow layout is designed rather than inherited: the scale is fluid rather than stepped. Motion has a reduced-motion branch, and the media carries a poster frame so the page still communicates when autoplay is unavailable. The mobile version is a decision, not a fallback.

faq.question: How is this Cortexa FAQ entry organised?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 4,955-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: How long is the prompt behind Cortexa FAQ?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1826x1302, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Can I rebuild the Cortexa FAQ FAQ section in a different stack?
faq.answer: Cortexa FAQ was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

audience: Quote a 1826x1302 frame in the handoff note so the next build does not have to re-derive it from the page.
